policy_prompt_for_subgoal: The cube slides back and forth along a line that passes through the target; every time it crosses the target line counts as one arrival at the target. The goal instruction names the ordinal N (second, third, fifth...). The button must be pressed one arrival early: when N-1 arrivals have happened and the cube is on its way back toward the target, so the press lands as the cube reaches the target for the Nth time. An episode starts in A: at the first step (empty memory, gripper raised out of the frame and not yet above the button) choose A 'move to the top of the button to prepare'. No point is needed. At every later step (gripper is already positioned above the button, fingers closed), first update memory as instructed, then decide using the updated crossings value and the cube motion in this step's frames: - Determine the cube's motion with a velocity-and-side test on the last two frames shown at this step, using their timesteps: v = (cube_x at the last frame - cube_x at the previous frame) / (last timestep - previous timestep), in pixels per timestep. Always divide by the time gap; the last pair of frames is often only a few timesteps apart, so never use the raw displacement. Take the cube's side at the last frame (smaller_x if cube_x < target_x, larger_x if cube_x > target_x). The cube is MOVING AWAY if it is on the larger_x side and v > +1, or on the smaller_x side and v < -1. In every other case the cube is NOT moving away: either |v| is at most 1 px per timestep (the cube is stopped or slowing at the turnaround at the far end of its swing, where the press, which takes long, lands as it swings back), or v points back toward the target line from the side the cube is on. If the two frames lie on different sides of the target, the cube has just crossed and is moving away on its new side; the test already says so, since the velocity sign and the new side agree. Do not use |cube_x - target_x| shrinking or growing as the test: it shrinks across a crossing even though the cube is then moving away. - Choose C 'press button to stop the cube' if crossings == N-1 AND the cube is NOT moving away by the test above (heading toward the target, or stopped/slowing at the turnaround with |v| at most 1 px per timestep). No point is needed. - Otherwise choose B 'remain static'. This covers: crossings < N-1 (even if the cube is heading toward the target, let it pass), and crossings == N-1 while the cube is MOVING AWAY by the test above, faster than 1 px per timestep (including the step right after the (N-1)th crossing, and while it is still running out toward the far end). If crossings somehow exceeds N-1, or the situation matches no rule above, choose C immediately if the cube is NOT moving away by the velocity-and-side test above, otherwise B. Never choose A after the first step.

fields.name: crossings
fields.description: Take the crossings count carried in (0 at the first step, since memory is empty). Build the sequence: the carried-in cube_side (skip if memory is empty), then the side (cube_x < target_x -> smaller_x, cube_x > target_x -> larger_x) of each frame shown at this step in time order, ending with the scene at this step. Add 1 for every consecutive pair in that sequence whose side differs. Write the result. e.g. 2

fields.name: cube_side
fields.description: The side of the target line the cube is on in the last frame shown at this step (the scene at this decision step): 'smaller_x' if cube_x < target_x, 'larger_x' if cube_x > target_x. Overwrite it every step. e.g. larger_x
